hook: A U.S. Air Force MISREP filed by the 482nd Attack Squadron (482ATKS) documenting a 20-hour armed reconnaissance mission over the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman on August 8–9, 2020, during which a single UAP was observed via Full Motion Video (FMV) at 0726Z while the aircraft conducted pattern-of-life ISR tasked by NAVCENT.
why_it_matters: This report illustrates how UAP encounters are embedded within routine military ISR operations and reported through standardized MISREP bureaucratic channels — the UAP sighting is one line item among Iranian vessel surveillance, SIGINT collection, and an Iranian Air Defense radio contact. The observation method (FMV only, with weather noted as intermittently degrading collection) raises questions about sensor corroboration, as no radar or additional sensor data is recorded for the UAP event itself. The document was approved for release to AARO in March 2026 under a batch declassification action covering MDR 26-0038 through 26-0046, indicating systematic rather than event-driven disclosure.

key_findings.finding: A single UAP was observed via FMV at 0726Z on August 8, 2020, described only as 'TRANSITTING' with no impact to mission. No additional sensor modalities (radar, SIGINT) are recorded for the UAP event.

key_findings.finding: Dense cloud coverage intermittently degraded FMV collection effectiveness during the mission, which is the sole sensor modality listed for the UAP observation, potentially limiting the quality of any imagery captured of the event.

key_findings.finding: The mission's primary purpose was ISR pattern-of-life collection against Iranian/IRGC vessels in the Arabian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman — not UAP investigation — and the intel gap was recorded as not filled despite the UAP observation.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document was explicitly approved for release to AARO on 03/27/26 under USCENTCOM MDR 26-0038 to MDR 26-0046, making AARO the direct institutional recipient and custodian of this UAP report.

Batch declassification under a USCENTCOM MDR series approved in March 2026 suggests a disclosure process likely tied to congressional oversight mandates for UAP reporting, though no direct congressional reference appears in the document.
